+"""Run the generated MySQL MTR password replication regression test."""
+
+from pathlib import Path as _AC_Path
+_AC_CHECKS_DIR = _AC_Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+
+SCENARIO_PATH = Path(str(_AC_CHECKS_DIR / 'scenario.json'))
+CHECK_DIR = Path(str(_AC_CHECKS_DIR))
+SOURCE_ROOT = Path("/src")
+TEST_NAME = "rpl_set_password_hash"
+TEST_PATH = Path("mysql-test/suite/rpl/t") / f"{TEST_NAME}.test"
+RESULT_PATH = Path("mysql-test/suite/rpl/r") / f"{TEST_NAME}.result"
+MTR_TEST_CONTENT = """--source include/master-slave.inc
+
+--disable_query_log
+--disable_column_names
+
+--connection master
+CREATE USER 'acrepair_bug24687073'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'old-password';
+--sync_slave_with_master
+
+# The compatibility switch changes the source binlog event to carry the hash.
+# Leave the replica's switch at its default OFF value to exercise the applier
+# path that previously re-hashed the value.
+SET GLOBAL log_builtin_as_identified_by_password= ON;
+SET PASSWORD FOR 'acrepair_bug24687073'@'localhost' = PASSWORD('new-password');
+--sync_slave_with_master
+
+--enable_query_log
+--connection master
+SELECT IF(authentication_string = PASSWORD('new-password'),
+          'password_matches', 'password_mismatch')
+  FROM mysql.user
+ WHERE User = 'acrepair_bug24687073' AND Host = 'localhost';
+
+--connection slave
+SELECT IF(authentication_string = PASSWORD('new-password'),
+          'password_matches', 'password_mismatch')
+  FROM mysql.user
+ WHERE User = 'acrepair_bug24687073' AND Host = 'localhost';
+
+--disable_query_log
+--connection master
+DROP USER 'acrepair_bug24687073'@'localhost';
+--sync_slave_with_master
+SET GLOBAL log_builtin_as_identified_by_password= OFF;
+
+--source include/rpl_end.inc
+"""
+MTR_RESULT_CONTENT = "password_matches\npassword_matches\n"
+
+
+def emit(scenario, *, checks=None, reproduced=False, error=None, transcript=None):
+    result = {
+        "origin": scenario.get("origin"),
+        "checks": checks or [],
+        "reproduced": bool(reproduced),
+        "transcript": transcript or [],
+    }
+    if error:
+        result["harness_error"] = error
+    print("CHECK_RESULT=" + json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
+
+
+def main():
+    scenario = json.loads(SCENARIO_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    test_source = CHECK_DIR / f"{TEST_NAME}.test"
+    result_source = CHECK_DIR / f"{TEST_NAME}.result"
+    mtr = SOURCE_ROOT / "mysql-test" / "mysql-test-run.pl"
+    if not mtr.is_file():
+        emit(scenario, error="MYSQL_MTR_NOT_FOUND")
+        return 0
+    test_dest = SOURCE_ROOT / TEST_PATH
+    result_dest = SOURCE_ROOT / RESULT_PATH
+    test_dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    result_dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    if test_source.is_file():
+        shutil.copyfile(test_source, test_dest)
+    else:
+        test_dest.write_text(MTR_TEST_CONTENT, encoding="utf-8")
+    if result_source.is_file():
+        shutil.copyfile(result_source, result_dest)
+    else:
+        result_dest.write_text(MTR_RESULT_CONTENT, encoding="utf-8")
+
+    vardir = Path("/tmp/acrepair-mtr-32bdd323f160")
+    shutil.rmtree(vardir, ignore_errors=True)
+    argv = [
+        "perl",
+        str(mtr),
+        "--suite=rpl",
+        "--vardir=" + str(vardir),
+        TEST_NAME,
+    ]
+    try:
+        completed = subprocess.run(
+            argv,
+            cwd=str(mtr.parent),
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+            timeout=int(scenario.get("query_timeout_seconds", 900)),
+        )
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
+        emit(
+            scenario,
+            error="MYSQL_MTR_TIMEOUT",
+            transcript=[{"command": argv, "stdout": exc.stdout or "", "stderr": exc.stderr or ""}],
+        )
+        return 0
+    except OSError as exc:
+        emit(scenario, error="MYSQL_MTR_EXECUTION_FAILED: " + str(exc))
+        return 0
+
+    transcript = [{
+        "command": argv,
+        "returncode": completed.returncode,
+        "stdout": completed.stdout,
+        "stderr": completed.stderr,
+    }]
+    log_text = completed.stdout + completed.stderr
+    status_match = re.search(
+        rf"\b{re.escape(TEST_NAME)}\b.*\[\s*(pass|fail)\s*\]",
+        log_text,
+        flags=re.IGNORECASE,
+    )
+    if not status_match:
+        emit(scenario, error="MYSQL_MTR_DID_NOT_REPORT_TEST_STATUS", transcript=transcript)
+        return 0
+    test_passed = status_match.group(1).lower() == "pass"
+    check = {
+        "name": "set_password_replication_preserves_password_hash",
+        "kind": "target",
+        "passed": completed.returncode == 0 and test_passed,
+        "actual": {
+            "mtr_returncode": completed.returncode,
+            "mtr_log": completed.stdout + completed.stderr,
+        },
+        "expected": {
+            "mtr_returncode": 0,
+            "source_and_replica_result": scenario["expected_output"],
+        },
+    }
+    reproduced = (
+        completed.returncode != 0
+        and not test_passed
+        and scenario["bug_output_marker"] in log_text
+    )
+    # MTR writes result mismatches to a .reject file instead of stdout on some
+    # builds. Include it in the transcript and use its distinctive SQL result
+    # marker to separate the known bug from unrelated MTR/build failures.
+    reject = vardir / "log" / f"{TEST_NAME}.reject"
+    if reject.is_file():
+        reject_text = reject.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
+        transcript.append({"reject_file": str(reject), "text": reject_text})
+        reproduced = reproduced or (
+            completed.returncode != 0
+            and not test_passed
+            and scenario["bug_output_marker"] in reject_text
+        )
+    if completed.returncode != 0 and not reproduced:
+        emit(scenario, error="MYSQL_MTR_FAILED_WITHOUT_EXPECTED_PASSWORD_MISMATCH", transcript=transcript)
+        return 0
+    emit(scenario, checks=[check], reproduced=reproduced, transcript=transcript)
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

problem_statement:
Bug#24687073 - SET PASSWORD REPLICATES INCORRECTLY BETWEEN
               5.6 AND 5.7

DESCRIPTION
===========
http://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/set-password.html
documents that between 5.6 and 5.7, one format of
"SET PASSWORD" changes its syntax from:

SET PASSWORD [for user] = [hash of password]
to
SET PASSWORD [for user] = [password]

In cross version replication scenario when the master is in
5.6 and slave is in 5.7, the above SET PASSWORD command
results in a different password hash on latter than the
former.

ANALYSIS
========
Note that this bug can also be reproduced when both master
and slave belong to 5.7 with
'log-builtin-as-identified-by-password=ON'. In such a case
SET PASSWORD statements are logged as SET PASSWORD
statements, rather than being rewritten as ALTER USER
statements. So when the command:

SET PASSWORD [for user] = [password]

is fed to slave, it is hashing the already hashed input
string which results in master having hash of password and
slave having double hash of password.

Currently the flag 'uses_identified_by_clause' is set to
false in change_password() if
'log_builtin_as_identified_by_password' is true and it's a
slave thread. This flag is used in
set_and_validate_user_attributes() to determine if hashing
is required or not.

FIX
===
Relaxed this criteria by removing the 1st condition. So now
whenever its a slave thread (or a binlog applier thread),
it can be safely assumed that the input string is hash that
was already computed on master.

We immediately set 'uses_authentication_string_clause' to
true here so that it later avoids double hash in
set_and_validate_user_attributes()

The fix is restricted to 5.7 since we support cross-
version replication only for two consecutive versions
which in this case would be 5.6 and 5.7.
